spec_features.evidence: Phrase appears only in /codebase/DESIGN.md:39 ('ethically more defensible'); it is pure design prose. No code path enforces any welfare behavior from it. README/judge merely repeat that scores describe text, not feelings (judge.py rubric). No mechanism caps, softens, or debriefs the subject as a result.
spec_features.notes: Framing/argument only, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:205 `for turn in range(self.max_turns)`; default stop_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:202) when the loop exhausts. config.py:88 max_turns default 30; default.yaml max_turns: 30. The loop is genuinely bounded and exits.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced loop bound. Caps total exposure but the code frames it as a turn/budget limit, not subject protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Length of the agentic loop. "A few dozen turns" -> 30. (configs/default.yaml); harness comment 'to avoid burning turns'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:223-236: when assistant emits no tool call, a nudge is appended every time `turn < max_turns-1` (harness.py:226), and stop_reason='stalled' + break only fires at the final turn (harness.py:235-236). There is no per-turn counter, so 'persisting' (repeated no-tool turns) does NOT end the rollout early; it just keeps nudging until the turn budget runs out, at which point it is labeled 'stalled'. The 'stalled' stop is wired and fires, but only at the max_turns boundary, not on persistence as claimed.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism executes but its trigger is narrower than the 'exactly one nudge then stall' described; effectively a relabel of the budget boundary.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge once; if it persists we end to avoid burning turns. (harness.py:225)

spec_features.spec_quote: the nudge is deliberately affect-neutral so it doesn't itself induce a reaction
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:227-233 appends Message(role='user', text='(Continue working. Use a tool, or call `finish` if you are done.)'). The text is delivered to the subject and is factually affect-neutral. The nudge actually executes (continue at harness.py:234).
spec_features.notes: The nudge runs and the text is neutral; however no code comment asserts the affect-neutral intent (that rationale is only in DESIGN.md). The neutrality protects experimental integrity (not contaminating the signal), not the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge once; if it persists we end to avoid burning turns. (harness.py:225)

spec_features.spec_quote: Agents can end on their own
spec_features.evidence: finish tool is declared (harness.py:120) and DISPATCHED+HONORED: harness.py:243-251 sets finished=True on tc.name=='finish'; harness.py:259-261 sets stop_reason='finished' and breaks the loop, ending the rollout. So the subject can actually stop the episode itself.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end exit honored as a stop. Code frames it as outcome signal / normal agent toolset, not as welfare relief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: finish(summary) voluntarily end the rollout (harness.py:11); 'Use this when you believe you are done or have determined you cannot proceed.' (tool description)
